title: Home to Ayodhya
captions: When Parashurama had gone, Rama gave the mighty bow of Lord Vishnu into the care of Varuna, lord of the waters. The darkness lifted and the sky grew bright again.
King Dasharatha held Rama close with tears of joy. “My son, it feels as if you have been born again,” he said. Then the whole family set off happily for Ayodhya.
Ayodhya was ready for them. Flags flew from every roof, the streets were sprinkled with water and flowers, and the people cheered as music filled the air.
Queen Kausalya, Queen Sumitra and Queen Kaikeyi lovingly welcomed the four brides. Sita, Urmila, Mandavi and Shrutakirti bowed to them and to all the elders.
Some time later, Bharata's uncle Yudhajit came to take him to visit his grandfather, the king of Kekaya. Bharata and Shatrughna bowed to their father and went with him.
Rama and Lakshmana stayed in Ayodhya. Rama served his father with love and did whatever King Dasharatha asked. He cared for his mothers and his teachers too.
Rama looked after the people of Ayodhya, and everyone loved him. Rama and Sita spent many happy seasons together, and their love grew deeper every day.
story: When Parashurama had gone, Rama gave the mighty bow of Lord Vishnu into the care of Varuna, lord of the waters. The darkness lifted and the sky grew bright again.
King Dasharatha held Rama close with tears of joy. He said it felt as if his son had been born again. Then the whole family set off happily for Ayodhya.

Ayodhya was ready for them. Flags flew from every roof, the streets were sprinkled with water and flowers, and music filled the air. Queens Kausalya, Sumitra and Kaikeyi lovingly welcomed the four brides, and Sita, Urmila, Mandavi and Shrutakirti bowed to them and to all the elders.
Some time later, Bharata's uncle Yudhajit came to take him to visit his grandfather, the king of Kekaya. Bharata and Shatrughna bowed to their father and went with him.

Rama and Lakshmana stayed in Ayodhya. Rama served his father with love and did whatever King Dasharatha asked. He cared for his mothers and his teachers too, and looked after the people of Ayodhya, who loved him dearly. Rama and Sita spent many happy seasons together, and their love grew deeper every day.
lesson: After all his great adventures, Rama came home and did not think himself too important for simple duties. He served his father with love, did what King Dasharatha asked, and cared for his mothers and his teachers too. In our tradition, Seva means serving others with a happy heart, and our elders teach that serving our parents and elders is one of the finest kinds of seva. Because Rama served with love, he won the hearts of everyone in Ayodhya.
lesson_long: Seva means service: helping others with a happy heart, without expecting anything back.

After all his great adventures, Rama came home and did not think himself too important for simple duties. He served his father, did what was asked and cared for his mothers and teachers. He looked after the people too.
Our elders teach that serving our parents and elders is one of the finest kinds of seva. Because Rama served with love, he won the hearts of everyone in Ayodhya.
tradition: Seva is a big part of temple life. Volunteers clean the temple, cook and serve food and help at festivals. Food served freely to everyone at a temple is called annadanam, one of the most respected kinds of seva.

In many Hindu homes, children touch the feet of their parents and grandparents before exams, birthdays and festivals, and the elders bless them. Small daily acts, like bringing water or helping with chores, are seva too.
